description: Master Django ORM, defining models, migrations, and relationships

slides.title: Introduction to Models
slides.content:
# Django Models 🗄️

Models are Python classes that define your database structure!

## What you'll learn:
- **ORM** - Object-Relational Mapping
- **Defining models** - Fields and options
- **Database migrations** - Schema changes
- **Model Relationships** - ForeignKey, ManyToMany

## Why Use Models?

```python
# Without ORM (raw SQL - error-prone, unsafe)
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", [user_id])
row = cursor.fetchone()

# With Django ORM (safe, readable, portable)
user = User.objects.get(id=user_id)
```

## Model = Database Table

```python
class Article(models.Model):    # → articles table
    title = models.CharField()   # → title column
    content = models.TextField() # → content column
    created = models.DateTimeField() # → created column
```

> 💡 **The ORM translates Python to SQL!** You write Python, Django generates optimized, database-specific SQL automatically.

slides.title: ORM - Object-Relational Mapping
slides.content:
# Understanding the ORM 🔄

The ORM is a bridge between Python objects and database tables.

## How it Works

```
Python Class  ←→  Database Table
Class Attribute ←→ Table Column
Class Instance ←→ Table Row
```

## ORM Benefits

### 1. Database Portability
```python
# Same code works with SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL
DATABASES = {
    'default': {
        'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.postgresql',  # Just change this!
        'NAME': 'mydb',
    }
}
```

### 2. SQL Injection Prevention
```python
# ORM automatically escapes inputs
User.objects.filter(username=user_input)  # Safe!
# vs raw SQL susceptible to injection
```

### 3. Pythonic Querying
```python
# Complex queries in readable Python
articles = Article.objects.filter(
    published__year=2024,
    category__name='Python',
    author__is_active=True
).order_by('-created')[:10]

# Django generates optimized SQL:
# SELECT ... FROM articles
# INNER JOIN categories ON ...
# INNER JOIN users ON ...
# WHERE ... ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 10
```

> 🎯 **ORM lets you think in objects, not SQL!**

slides.title: Defining Models - Part 1
slides.content:
# Creating Models 📝 (Part 1)

## Basic Model Structure

```python
# models.py
from django.db import models

class Article(models.Model):
    # Fields define columns
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True)
    content = models.TextField()
    excerpt = models.TextField(max_length=500, blank=True)
    
    # Timestamps
    published = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
    
    # Boolean
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    is_featured = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    
    # String representation
    def __str__(self):
        return self.title
    
    # Metadata
    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-published']  # Default ordering
        verbose_name_plural = 'Articles'
```

## Common Field Types

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| `CharField` | Short text (max_length required) | title, name |
| `TextField` | Long text (unlimited) | content, description |
| `IntegerField` | Integers | count, age |
| `DecimalField` | Precise decimals | price, rating |
| `BooleanField` | True/False | is_active |
| `DateField` | Date only | birth_date |
| `DateTimeField` | Date and time | created_at |
| `EmailField` | Validated email | email |
| `URLField` | Validated URL | website |

slides.title: Defining Models - Part 2
slides.content:
# Creating Models 📝 (Part 2)

## Field Options

```python
class Product(models.Model):
    # Required vs Optional
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)  # Required by default
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)  # Optional in forms
    
    # Null values
    category = models.CharField(max_length=50, null=True)  # NULL in DB
    
    # Default values
    price = models.DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2, default=0.00)
    in_stock = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    
    # Unique constraint
    sku = models.CharField(max_length=50, unique=True)
    
    # Choices
    STATUS_CHOICES = [
        ('draft', 'Draft'),
        ('published', 'Published'),
        ('archived', 'Archived'),
    ]
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=STATUS_CHOICES, default='draft')
    
    # Help text (shown in forms)
    notes = models.TextField(blank=True, help_text='Internal notes')
```

## More Field Types

```python
# Files and Images
image = models.ImageField(upload_to='products/')
document = models.FileField(upload_to='docs/')

# JSON data
metadata = models.JSONField(default=dict)

# UUID
id = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)

# Slug (URL-friendly text)
slug = models.SlugField(max_length=100, unique=True)
```

> 💡 **`blank=True`** affects forms (optional field), **`null=True`** affects database (allows NULL).

slides.title: Database Migrations
slides.content:
# Migrations 🔄

Migrations track changes to your models and apply them to the database.

## Migration Workflow

```bash
# Step 1: Make changes to your models.py

# Step 2: Create migration files
python manage.py makemigrations
# Output: Migrations for 'blog':
#   blog/migrations/0001_initial.py
#     - Create model Article

# Step 3: Apply migrations to database
python manage.py migrate
# Output: Applying blog.0001_initial... OK
```

## Viewing Migrations

```bash
# See all migrations and their status
python manage.py showmigrations
# blog
#  [X] 0001_initial
#  [X] 0002_add_category
#  [ ] 0003_add_tags   ← Not applied yet

# See SQL that will be executed
python manage.py sqlmigrate blog 0001
# BEGIN;
# CREATE TABLE "blog_article" (...)
# COMMIT;
```

## Migration Commands

```bash
# Rollback to specific migration
python manage.py migrate blog 0001

# Rollback all migrations for an app
python manage.py migrate blog zero

# Create migration with custom name
python manage.py makemigrations blog --name add_article_views
```

> ⚠️ **Always commit migration files to version control!** They're essential for team collaboration and deployment.

slides.title: Model Relationships - ForeignKey
slides.content:
# Relationships 🔗 (Part 1)

## ForeignKey (One-to-Many)

One category has many articles.

```python
class Category(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True)
    
    def __str__(self):
        return self.name

class Article(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    category = models.ForeignKey(
        Category,
        on_delete=models.CASCADE,  # Delete articles if category deleted
        related_name='articles'    # Access from category: category.articles.all()
    )
```

## on_delete Options

| Option | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `CASCADE` | Delete related objects too |
| `PROTECT` | Prevent deletion (raise error) |
| `SET_NULL` | Set foreign key to NULL |
| `SET_DEFAULT` | Set to default value |
| `DO_NOTHING` | Do nothing (database may error) |

## Using ForeignKey

```python
# Creating with relationship
category = Category.objects.get(name='Python')
article = Article.objects.create(
    title='Learn Django',
    category=category
)

# Forward relation (article → category)
article.category.name  # 'Python'

# Reverse relation (category → articles)
category.articles.all()  # All articles in this category
category.articles.count()  # Number of articles
```

slides.title: Model Relationships - ManyToMany
slides.content:
# Relationships 🔗 (Part 2)

## ManyToManyField

An article can have many tags, a tag can be on many articles.

```python
class Tag(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    
    def __str__(self):
        return self.name

class Article(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(
        Tag,
        related_name='articles',
        blank=True  # Optional
    )
```

## Working with ManyToMany

```python
# Add tags to article
article = Article.objects.get(pk=1)
python_tag = Tag.objects.get(name='Python')
django_tag = Tag.objects.get(name='Django')

article.tags.add(python_tag, django_tag)

# Remove tag
article.tags.remove(python_tag)

# Clear all tags
article.tags.clear()

# Set specific tags (replaces all)
article.tags.set([tag1, tag2])

# Query through relationship
article.tags.all()  # All tags on article
python_tag.articles.all()  # All articles with this tag

# Filter using relationship
Article.objects.filter(tags__name='Python')
```

## OneToOneField

```python
# One user has one profile
class Profile(models.Model):
    user = models.OneToOneField(
        User,
        on_delete=models.CASCADE,
        related_name='profile'
    )
    bio = models.TextField()
    avatar = models.ImageField(upload_to='avatars/')

# Access: user.profile.bio
```

slides.title: QuerySet API - CRUD
slides.content:
# QuerySet API 🔍

## Create

```python
# Method 1: create() - saves immediately
article = Article.objects.create(
    title='My Article',
    content='Hello World',
    category=category
)

# Method 2: save() - more control
article = Article(title='My Article', content='Hello')
article.save()  # Explicit save

# Bulk create (efficient for many objects)
Article.objects.bulk_create([
    Article(title='Article 1', content='...'),
    Article(title='Article 2', content='...'),
])
```

## Read

```python
# Get all objects
articles = Article.objects.all()

# Get single object
article = Article.objects.get(pk=5)  # Raises DoesNotExist if not found

# Filter (returns QuerySet)
active = Article.objects.filter(is_active=True)
python_articles = Article.objects.filter(title__contains='Python')

# Exclude
not_drafts = Article.objects.exclude(status='draft')

# First/Last
first = Article.objects.first()
last = Article.objects.last()

# Check existence
if Article.objects.filter(pk=5).exists():
    print('Found!')
```

## Update & Delete

```python
# Update single object
article = Article.objects.get(pk=5)
article.title = 'New Title'
article.save()

# Bulk update (efficient)
Article.objects.filter(is_active=False).update(is_active=True)

# Delete single object
article.delete()

# Bulk delete
Article.objects.filter(status='draft').delete()
```

slides.title: QuerySet API - Field Lookups
slides.content:
# Field Lookups 🎯

Powerful filtering with double underscores!

## Comparison Lookups

```python
# Greater than / Less than
Article.objects.filter(views__gt=100)    # views > 100
Article.objects.filter(views__gte=100)   # views >= 100
Article.objects.filter(views__lt=100)    # views < 100
Article.objects.filter(views__lte=100)   # views <= 100

# Exact match (default)
Article.objects.filter(status='published')  # Same as status__exact

# In list
Article.objects.filter(status__in=['published', 'featured'])

# Range
Article.objects.filter(views__range=(100, 1000))
```

## Text Lookups

```python
# Contains (case-sensitive)
Article.objects.filter(title__contains='Python')

# Contains (case-insensitive)
Article.objects.filter(title__icontains='python')

# Starts/ends with
Article.objects.filter(title__startswith='How')
Article.objects.filter(title__iendswith='?')

# Exact (case-insensitive)
Article.objects.filter(title__iexact='python basics')
```

## Date Lookups

```python
# Extract year/month/day
Article.objects.filter(published__year=2024)
Article.objects.filter(published__month=3)
Article.objects.filter(published__day=15)

# Date ranges
from datetime import date
Article.objects.filter(published__date=date.today())
Article.objects.filter(published__gte=date(2024, 1, 1))
```

## Null/Empty Checks

```python
Article.objects.filter(category__isnull=True)   # No category
Article.objects.filter(content__isnull=False)   # Has content
```

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Excellent Work! 🎉

You've mastered Django Models!

## ORM
- ✅ Maps Python classes to database tables
- ✅ Database-agnostic code
- ✅ Protection from SQL injection

## Defining Models
- ✅ Field types: CharField, TextField, IntegerField, etc.
- ✅ Field options: blank, null, default, choices
- ✅ `__str__` method for display
- ✅ Meta class for model options

## Database Migrations
- ✅ `makemigrations` - Create migration files
- ✅ `migrate` - Apply to database
- ✅ `showmigrations` - View status

## Model Relationships
- ✅ ForeignKey (One-to-Many)
- ✅ ManyToManyField (Many-to-Many)
- ✅ OneToOneField (One-to-One)
- ✅ `on_delete` options
- ✅ `related_name` for reverse access

## QuerySet API
- ✅ CRUD: create, get, filter, update, delete
- ✅ Field lookups: `__contains`, `__gt`, `__year`, etc.
- ✅ Chaining querysets

> 🚀 **Next Steps:** Learn about Forms for user input!
